old_title: Europe wildfires latest: Winds cause blazes to spread faster as 300,000 evacuated
new_title: Europe wildfires latest: Firefighters warn blaze near Bordeaux could last months
old_text:
Overnight winds have caused wildfires across Spain and France to spread even faster, according to local authorities.
Officials in Gironde said that the flames in the region were fed by winds accelerating the fire, after Spanish officials had also warned this could be the case on Saturday.
One man has died in a wildfire in Manises, near the Spanish city of Valencia, the country's interior ministry has said.
He was found in a car in a ravine hundreds of kilometres away from the severe wildfires spreading near to the Spanish capital Madrid.
Around 300,000 people have been displaced including some 70,000 people evacuated in central Spain.
Residents in western France have described the scenes as "totally apocalyptic" after fires in the village of Saumos destroyed more than 100 homes.
"The fires which are hitting our country have reached a level that has never been seen before," French prime minister Sebastien Lecornu wrote on X on Saturday.
Wildfires are also affecting parts of Scotland with a major incident declared in Cairngorms National Park .
Mapped: The areas in France and Spain affected by raging wildfires
Over 280,000 people have been forced to evacuate their homes as wildfires continue to rage across Spain and France.
Government officials from both countries have commented on the historic nature of the blaze, with Madrid's regional president Isabel Díaz Ayuso describing it "the worst fire in the history of the region".
"The fires which are hitting our country have reached a level that has never been seen before," French prime minister Sebastien Lecornu wrote on X on Saturday.
Lecornu promised that over 1.5 million face masks would be provided as even areas unaffected by the worst of the blaze saw air quality deteriorate and smoke spread.
Below we look at the areas affected and evacuated as a result of the wildfires.
Bordeaux officials considering 'total evacuation' of city
Bordeaux City Council is exploring options to deal with the various ways the wildfires nearby could evolve, including a total evacuation of the city, a spokesperson told Sky News.
The Council is "currently studying scenarios for all possible ways the fire could evolve", they said, which includes a total evacuation of the city, if needed.
Surrounding areas have been evacuated as the fire advanced amid high winds. The city is the sixth largest in France.
Oregon fire looms near town as fourth firefighter dies weeks after Colorado blaze
As dry, windy weather fueled a big wildfire near a city in central Oregon, a fourth firefighter died after he and several colleagues last month were overcome by a fast-moving wildfire near the Colorado-Utah border, authorities said Saturday.
Nathan Matthews, 43, of Lincoln, Nebraska, died Friday, the federal Interior Department said in a statement. Meanwhile, several fierce wildfires in a summer of big ones continued burning across the western US.
One of the worst - and the one deemed top priority for firefighting efforts - was just a few miles (5km) north of Sisters, a central Oregon city of about 3,000 people.
Wildfire spreads to northeastern Algerian province
A wildfire spread in Haddada municipality in Algeria's northeastern Souk Ahras province on Saturday, as firefighters responded to the blaze.
High winds make fighting Spanish wildfires harder, officials say
Winds in Spain with gusts of up to 60kmph (38mph) are complicating the fight against out-of-control wildfires west of Madrid.
Two separate wildfires in the Madrid region combined on Friday and became one huge blaze, but so far they have not merged with another in Avila, in the neighbouring Castilla y Leon region.
The fires have so far forced more than 30,000 people to flee their homes in the Madrid region and more than 20,000 to be confined at home, the ministry said on Saturday, in what officials have called the region's worst fire on record.
Overnight weather conditions had helped the firefighters.
"The change in weather conditions (less wind, higher humidity, and lower temperature) has greatly benefited the fight against the forest fires, which have advanced little and decreased in intensity," the central government in Madrid said on Saturday morning.
Plumes of thick smoke could be seen in the sky west of the capital. More than 9,000 hectares have burned in the wildfires in the Madrid region, authorities said.
Sunday's grand finale of Tour de France to be shortened
Sunday's grand finale of the Tour de France, ending in Paris, will be shortened due to the impact of security forces being redeployed to battle wildfires near Bordeaux, organisers and police said.
The Tour's final leg - Stage 21 when cyclists enter Paris and do laps around the Champs Elysees - will be shortened to 89km instead of the 133km originally planned.
"As numerous wildfires are currently affecting France, particularly the Gironde region, emergency services are fully mobilised to combat the blazes, while internal security forces are working to secure the affected areas and protect the population," the Paris police and the event's organisers said in a joint statement.
"In light of this, the Interior Ministry has decided to redeploy a portion of the internal security forces initially mobilised to ensure security for the final stage of the Tour de France, in order to reinforce the response efforts in the areas affected by the wildfires."
Wildfire leads to evacuations in some suburbs of the French city of Bordeaux
Authorities in France evacuated some suburbs of Bordeaux on Saturday as a massive wildfire shifted toward the city famous for its wines.
The prefect of the Gironde region that includes Bordeaux ordered the evacuation in the early hours of Saturday, covering parts of three of the city's western suburbs, including its airport.
new_text:
Gironde authorities have warned that they could be fighting raging blazes near Bordeaux for "several weeks or even several months".
The "real challenge is endurance" according to Lieutenant Colonel David Annotel, spokesperson for the National Firefighters Federation of France who told Franceinfo.
He reflected that the 2022 Landiras wildfire was not considered officially extinguished until 2025.
"We're looking at a similar situation. For many weeks and months, crews from all over France will have to continue rotating in."
Bordeaux Airport's hotel zone has been evacuated until further notice as raging wildfires threaten the city, although the airport itself remains operational.
In a statement overnight, the airport said while flights are still operational, no accommodation can be provided at the airport itself, which closes overnight.
It advised travellers to look outside the evacuated areas or at the Parc des Expositions.
Raging wildfires are now just 15km (9 miles) from Bordeaux, the city's mayor Thomas Cazenave said on Sunday.
It is the sixth largest city in France when including both the city proper and surrounding metropolitan area, and is home to over 1.2 million people.
Fire remains 'active and uncontrolled' but 'slowed down' overnight
Madrid authorities have said that wildfires raging near the capital remain "active and uncontrolled".
"The fires in the Community of Madrid during the night have slowed in their advance and have allowed firefighting teams to act on them," read a statement by the government delegation of Spain in the community of Madrid on Monday.
"The fire remains active and uncontrolled. 3 fronts have been identified, with the most active one located north of the San Juan Reservoir.
"Citizens are urged to continue exercising extreme caution and to stay informed about the situation's evolution through official sources."
Watch: Aerial footage shows shocking scale of forest fires outside Bordeaux
Wildfires have hit French economy like a 'clap of thunder', says minister
Wildfires in France have shocked the regional community French finance minister Roland Lescure said on Monday.
"It's like a clap of thunder for an area which could have done without this," Lescure told reporters.
Local blogger Ira Szmuk told The Independent that tourist cancellations will impact many in Bordeaux city.
"People aren't speaking about it yet because we're still in a life-threatening situation but for many people their whole year's revenue depends on these months. The year is over for us the moment you take summer away."
Watch: Distant wildfire almost engulfs home in just 8 minutes in chilling CCTV
Firefighters could be fighting blaze 'for months', warn Gironde authorities
Gironde authorities have warned that they could be fighting raging blazes near Bordeaux for "several weeks or even several months", Lieutenant Colonel David Annotel, spokesperson for the National Firefighters Federation of France told Franceinfo.
He said that the "real challenge is endurance" and reflected that the 2022 Landiras wildfire was not considered officially extinguished until 2025.
"We're looking at a similar situation. For many weeks and months, crews from all over France will have to continue rotating in."
UK preparing for wildfires similar to those that have torn through France and Spain, minister confirms
The government is preparing for wildfires in the UK similar to those that have torn through France and Spain this summer, a minister has confirmed.
Blazes have wrought destruction in mainland Europe this week, with 220,000 forced out of their homes in south-west France and 116,000 evacuated in Spain.
Around 42,000 hectares have been burnt in southwest France, in one of the largest forest fires since the Second World War. Since the start of the year, about 98,000 hectares have been scorched. Meanwhile, in Spain around 70,000 hectares have burned this year.
Asked whether the UK is preparing for similar events, minister for intergovernmental relations Hamish Falconer told Sky News: "Obviously there are wildfires in Scotland as well, and we're in touch with the Scottish government about what support the British government can provide.
Evacuation of Bordeaux 'not on the agenda' says government spokesperson
A complete evacuation of the city of Bordeaux is "not on the agenda" at this time, a government spokesperson told Franceinfo on Monday.
She added that the blaze was "very difficult to anticipate" and that the government "remains extremely cautious" about the "extraordinary fire".
Over the weekend, Bordeaux City Council told Sky News that it was considering a total evacuation of the city as one of the possible options in dealing with the fire.
Rain offers respite in small village outside of Bordeaux
Jérôme Steffe, the mayor of Cestas, a small rural village outside of Bordeaux, has said the situation has approved following rain overnight.
"We're lucky because we had rain during the night and the wind lessened a bit. That did a lot of good, but make no mistake: it's not because the leaves on the trees are damp and the flames have died down in places that there's no longer any risk," he said.
Gironde authorities said that "the situation remained stable overall during the night" but that firefighters continued to battle the blazes.
Firefighters battled throughout the night to keep fires away from Bordeaux
Firefighters battled throughout the night and into Monday morning to tackle raging wildfires threatening the city of Bordeaux.
About 220,000 people have been evacuated in France and more than 75,000 people have been evacuated in Spain with a further 30,000 ordered to shelter in place.
"This is a fire of a size never seen before," said Jerome Steffe, mayor of Cestas, on Monday. Cestas is one of the suburbs that lies just outside the main Bordeaux city area and from where thousands have had to be evacuated from homes and holiday residences.
The blazes, which broke out last week near the Atlantic coast, are now 15 km (10 miles) away from entry points to the main metropolitan area of Bordeaux.
A major risk is that temperatures in Bordeaux are set to rise to 37 degrees Celsius (98.6 degrees Fahrenheit) later this week, according to forecasts from France's weather office.
"It's a race against time before the heatwave returns," added Steffe.
